text.p: Openers Michael Atherton and Mark Butcher guided England from the possibility of defeat to the probability of a draw on the final day of the second test at Lord's on Monday.
The pair shared an opening partnership of 162, before Atherton trod on his off-stump playing back to Michael Kasprowicz after scoring 77.
At the tea interval, England were 169 for one with Butcher on 66 and his brother-in-law Alec Stewart on three.
Australia clearly fancied their chances of forcing a win to square the six-test Ashes series, even though so much time had been lost on the first four days through persistent heavy showers.
Mark Taylor declared at the overnight first innings total of 213 for seven, a lead of 136, and threw the new ball to Glenn McGrath when play began on time on a cloudy but mercifully dry morning.
But this time McGrath could not extract the life and movement he conjured during his eight for 38 in England's first innings 77, although both he and Paul Reiffel gave Butcher a torrid time.

Butcher, whose test place was in jeopardy after three successive failures and and two missed catches on Saturday, was lucky to survive a chance to Taylor at first slip off Reiffel when he had scored only two.

He could also make little of Shane Warne, deploying his wrist spin from the Nursery end, but fought doggedly to bring up his maiden test half-century with his seventh boundary, an edge through slips of Steve Waugh.
Atherton's half century, his 33rd in tests and 13th against Australia, was a typically obstinate offering, with most of his runs coming through pushes to leg.
He was severe on anything loose, playing handsome drives through the covers off McGrath and Reiffel and dismissing Michael Bevan's unorthodox left-arm spin for successive boundaries.
